description: PECT is a Python tool from the SSESLab electricity and environment project for estimating indirect environmental effects of grid electricity. A user specifies a United States location and time interval. The script obtains generation mix from WattTime and combines it with fuel-specific factors from EPA eGRID and other cited sources. Outputs are time series of generation by fuel, carbon and air-pollutant emissions, and water consumption and withdrawal estimates. Its geographic coverage is limited to United States regions represented by the input services; temporal resolution follows the requested interval and available fuel-mix data. Source, examples and notebooks are public under LGPL-3.0, so the code is free to obtain. Running it requires a separate WattTime account, and the repository advises using current eGRID factors. PECT could help compare electricity scenarios or estimate water and emissions consequences of building electricity demand. Its factors and grid-mix inputs can become stale, and no live API output was checked. The related catalogue record data-epa-egrid-emissions-generation-resource-integrated-database describes one input dataset. No code or service was run.
inputs: United States location and time interval
WattTime fuel-mix data and eGRID emission factors
name: PECT Power Externality Correlation Tool
notes: G5 G5-0975. Running PECT requires a valid WattTime API account and sufficiently current eGRID factors. No sign-in was needed for metadata review, and no API credentials were sought or used. The code licence is LGPL-3.0; third-party data-service terms were not checked. The model was not run.
